data.content_ref: inline:SRC_003's claim permits resumption when framing 'can deterministically quarantine the truncated bytes of a partial event' and refuses only when framing 'lacks the delimiters or checksums to deterministically distinguish a complete event from a partial one.' This framework addresses only the partial-vs-complete structural distinction. A structurally complete but logically uncommitted event (e.g., valid checksum, full body, but no commit record) is distinguishable from a partial, so SRC_003 would classify it as a complete event and permit resumption — yet treating an uncommitted event as committed corrupts the append-only identity of recorded events. SRC_003 never considers the distinction between structural completeness and logical commitment, leaving a resumption-permitting gap the problem's 'exactly when' standard requires closed.
